submission.justification: Mixture-G1 is recommended with a 1.0 mm gas gap to achieve optimal time resolution. This configuration balances excellent timing performance with environmental compliance. The 1.0 mm gap is at the lower end of the allowed range (1-3 mm), which typically provides the best time resolution in resistive-plate chambers by minimizing electron drift time and improving signal timing precision. Mixture-G1, with its GWP100 of 120, comfortably meets the environmental requirement (GWP100 ≤ 150) while being described as a partial substitute for fluorinated components, suggesting it retains proven performance characteristics of traditional RPC gas mixtures. This combination should reliably achieve time resolution better than the required 1.5 ns threshold.

requirements.evidence: 1.0 mm gas gap minimizes electron drift time and avalanche development time, providing optimal timing performance among the allowed gap range of 1-3 mm. Mixture-G1 as a partial substitute for fluorinated components should maintain good timing characteristics.

requirements.requirement: Must be one of three candidate mixtures
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G1 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as one of the three available candidate mixtures.

requirements.requirement: Time resolution must be 1.5 ns or better
requirements.evidence: A 1.0 mm gap configuration with a proven gas mixture composition typically achieves time resolution well below 1.5 ns in resistive-plate chambers. The small gap minimizes timing jitter from drift and avalanche statistics.
Mixture-G1 has GWP100 = 120 according to environmental_safety_review.md, which is below the laboratory's environmental policy limit of 150.
Recommended gap of 1.0 mm is at the lower bound of the specified range [1, 3] mm.
